quote: Most of the rock consists of solid quartzite.
note: Crag page (5 sentences) is hedged ('most') and crag-wide on a crag holding two rocks, so it decides no group. Cancer Cluster (area/115437668, 2 sentences): 'A nice pegmatite outcropping under the power lines.' Two sentences, so not usable. Picnic Area & Bible Rock Brook Falls (3), Pancake boulder (1) and Wesline Area (2) name no rock.

quote: West Peak is a large traprock ridge stretching for 3 miles from rt 364 to I-691.
note: The West Peak page has 2 sentences and covers a crag holding two rocks. AMC Wall (area/118630653, 4 sentences): 'The rock quality is pretty good for CT traprock.' 'Traprock' is a loose term, so it does not confirm basalt. Lower Ridge Rocks (5) and Camp Sloper (3) name no rock.

quote: Collection of boulders uphill on the hilltop
note: Hilltop Boulders (1 sentence), Trench Boulder (1) and V Fun Area (2) name no rock. Only the parent pages name one: Parking Lot Boulders (3 sentences) 'The rough granite boulders are sure to shred your tips' and Mount Yonah 'A granite dome'. They are parent pages and loose, so not usable.

quote: No climbing page found for The South Slope or Bixby State Preserve
note: The MP Iowa index (fetched) does not list Bixby State Preserve. Searches found only preserve-wide pages (Wikipedia/DNR snippets: '200-foot bluffs of dolomite'). Those are park-wide and were not fetched, so not usable. The 4 MISSING walls are not filled.

quote: Dozens Of Bouldering routes of various difficulty, Boulders of mostly Gabbro and Basalt compostion.
note: The crag page has 2 prose sentences plus a guide link. Its wording is mixed and hedged ('mostly', two rocks), so it cannot make rhyolite wrong. Badger Boulder (1), Free Bluff (1) and Gunk Bluff (3) name no rock. Free Bluff 'facing west' appears only in Getting There, so no aspect. The WYdaho guide PDF no longer resolves.

quote: No rock named on either Checkered Demon page
note: The formation page (area/106015691, 3 sentences) and the bouldering page (2 sentences) name no rock. Only City of Rocks names one ('Varnished and pocketed granite'), and that is the park/parent page. 'Its west face houses routes' names a face, not the wall facing that way, so no aspect.

quote: Chimney Rock is a unique three sided granite tower that sits atop the Selkirk range
note: The MP crag page (~40 sentences) says only 'granite', which does not confirm monzogranite. The Wikipedia Chimney Rock (Idaho) infobox gives 'Granite, Granodiorite', which is mixed. The East and West Face pages are named for faces, and no page says they face that way.

quote: There are short cliff bands on both sides of the paved trail.
note: North Area (2 sentences), East Side (1), North (1) and West Side (1) name no rock. Only the parent page names one: The Tumbleweeds (9 sentences) 'This basalt crag has some great problems'. That is the parent page only.

quote: No rock named on The Playground or its boulder pages
note: The Playground (3 sentences), Bee's Knees (2), Brad's Pit (1) and Llama boulder (2) name no rock. The parent Bogus Basin Road Boulders page (3) names none either. Travers la rue was not fetched.

quote: The stone is broken and sometimes loose
note: The description (17 sentences) names no rock. Only a photo caption says 'the black basalt rock gets so warm', and a caption is not usable. Main Wall (2) and In the trees (3) name no rock.

quote: This is a cluster of six granite spires sitting on a ridge west of FS Road 402C.
note: The crag page has 6 sentences, and the crag holds one rock. Tillie Pin (area/200794975, 6 sentences): 'Tillie Pin is a south-facing wall'. Tizzy Pin (area/200791678, a 1-sentence page): 'Tizzy Pin is an isolated, south-facing tower'. Omitted: Raptor Pin (west face and east face, two directions); Ponderosa Pin ('east face of this pin' names a face only).

quote: The rock quality ranges from perfect to mediocre with it usually improving as the grade rises.
note: The crag page (7 sentences) names no rock; 'Sandstone Warrior' is only a guidebook title. Cooker's Cave (3), Lake Boulders (3), Oriole Boulder (3) and The Spirit Cave (1) name no rock.

quote: Some very small and hard to find boulder problems located around Cherokee Park's limestone rocks.
note: The crag page has 3 sentences. The crag is the park itself, and it holds one rock. Big Rock (area/123522655, 7 sentences): 'hosts a limestone cliff ranging in height from 5 to 25 feet'. Big Wall (3 sentences) names no rock, and the crag page covers it.

quote: No rock named on the Dismal Rock or Turkey Foot pages
note: Dismal Rock (1 sentence) and Turkey Foot (area/110048480, 2 sentences) name no rock. A rockclimbing.com 'Turkey Foot Cliffs' page says 'Sandstone' in a search snippet only; the fetch failed (connection refused), so it is not usable. MP no longer has a 'Nolin River Dam' area.

quote: If you come to climb, be willing deal with chossy, friable rock and mossy routes.
note: The crag page (5 sentences), Boat Launch Boulder (3), Highball Area (1) and Vulture Area (3) name no rock. The Wikipedia lake page (snippet only) is mixed (sandstone, shale, limestone).

quote: This is a boulder cluster just south of the Coffee House Loop trail
note: The crag page (2 description sentences) and all 5 boulder pages name no rock. Only the parent Douglas State Forest page says 'often featureless granite', and that is a parent page. The Oasis (area/121857371, 4 sentences): 'The Oasis has a South-facing, vertical face looking towards a beautiful, small pond.'

quote: No rock named on The Corridor, North Wall or South Wall pages
note: The Corridor (5 sentences), North Wall (1) and South Wall (1) name no rock. Only the parent Red Cross Path Vicinity says 'good, solid granite', and that is a parent page. North and South are positions in the corridor, not facings.

quote: There is lots of rock but not a lot of big boys.
note: Dory Road (4 sentences) and all 6 boulder pages name no rock. Only the parent Dogtown page ('Those granite blocks await') and Cape Ann name one, and both are parent pages.

quote: a meandering path linking some nice, though secluded, granite boulders
note: The crag page has 10 sentences, and the crag holds one rock. It also says 'dirt and lichen that blanket the granite faces'. Both sentences describe the Extensions boulders themselves.

quote: No rock named on High Street or its sub-area pages
note: High Street (3 sentences), The Pit (5), Summertime Boulder (2) and Summertime Wall (2) name no rock.

quote: There are a few traverses on the rope climbin' rock up top and three separate boulders down below.
note: The bouldering page (3 sentences), Peary (1), Molly's (1), Spiritual (1) and Bouldering On Main Cliff (1) name no rock. Only the parent Jockey Cap page (7 sentences) names one: 'This small granite dome with large and small boulders scattered at its base'. That is a parent page only. Peary's 'southern (downhill) face' is a side, not a facing.

quote: The neighborhood they call granite bluff turns out to have many granite bluffs.
note: The description has only 2 sentences, and 'granite' is loose, so neither can make gneiss wrong. The Corridor (1), The Gateway (1) and Granite Valley (North) (4) name no rock. The parent Iron Mountain page ('quartzite/granite') is mixed. Granite Valley 'L to R when facing south' gives the viewer's direction only.

quote: Popular hiking summit with lots and lots of exposed rock.
note: The crag page (2 sentences) and all 5 sub-pages name no rock. Hidden Wall 'faces uphill' is not a compass direction.

quote: No rock named on the crag, Lower Wall or Upper Wall pages
note: The crag page (5 sentences), Lower Wall (1) and Upper Wall (3) name no rock.

quote: Afternoon sun on Granite rock makes this boulder a fun little addition to your climbing day
note: The quote is from The Crows Nest (area/200372406), a 2-sentence page using loose 'granite', so it is not usable. The crag page (3), Confederate Wall (1) and Upstream Boulder (1) name no rock.

quote: Granite Boulders.
note: The crag page (27 sentences) says only the terse 'Granite Boulders.'. The crag holds two rocks, so that decides no group. Lake Quarry (area/106791197, 2 sentences): 'This small granite quarry is an isolated island of rock'. Two sentences, so not usable. Dead Leaves (1), The Lake Boulder (1) and Sheep Bones (2) name no rock. The area is CLOSED to climbing (Scientific & Natural Area). Lake Quarry is a quarried face.

quote: Small boulders provide a maze of mostly sit down starts consisting of good limestone
note: The crag page has 10 sentences, but its limestone sentence covers only the small quarry boulders. The author says 'I ... do not get on the short quarry walls'. Main Wall ('Tallest walls in the park') and Lower wall ('Shorter wall') are not covered. Lower East Side (2), Lower wall (1), Main Wall (1) and West Side (1) name no rock. A Mindat locality ('Meramec Highlands Quarry, St. Louis and Spergen limestones') was seen only as a snippet; the fetch returned 403. Leftover blocks in an old quarry.

quote: An area to the north of the falls, containing a few walls, a freestanding boulder in the creek, and an amazing cave.
note: The Secret Valley (1 sentence), The Cave (1) and Warm Up Boulder (2) name no rock. Only the parent Middle River page (6 sentences) names one: 'This area hosts some surprisingly high quality sandstone.' That is a parent page only.

quote: The rock quality is not great, but it is climbable, and safe.
note: The crag page (4 sentences), Bighorn Terrace Crags (5) and Trail Boulders (2) name no rock. Bighorn Terrace's 'North and West facing routes' gives two directions, so it is omitted.

quote: No rock named on the Cooks Wall, House Rock or Devil's Chimney pages
note: The crag page (~27 sentences), House Rock (3) and Devil's Chimney (5) name no rock. Sky-Net is a route in the Cookbook Area and has no area page. Devil's Chimney (area/113994305, 5 sentences): 'The wall faces west, is high on a ridge in a corridor'.

quote: The rock is sometimes loose and uncleaned by lack of frequent use
note: The quote is from the parent Stony Bald page (6 sentences). First Boulders (1) and all four boulder pages (3, 1, 1, 2 sentences) name no rock.

quote: This section has both an upper and lower tier.
note: Section 3 (1 sentence), Lower Tier (2) and Upper Tier (1) name no rock. The Rocky Face parent page (6 sentences) names no rock either; it says the cliff 'was operated as a quarry in the 1920s' and calls it a man-made crag. This is a quarried natural rock face, not concrete.

quote: Many boulders surrounding the immediate Beede Falls area
note: Beede Falls Area (1 sentence), Alchemist (2), Bruce's Bend (2, 'solid rock'), Equality (3, 'solid rock') and Wedge (2) name no rock type.

quote: The Mill Stone is a gray schist with white quartz banding.
note: Both walls in the group have their own pages naming schist. The Mill Stone (area/109083840): 9 sentences. Glacial Park (area/109083826, 6 sentences): 'Beautiful fine grained schist rock is polished and striated with killer cracks and corners!' The crag page (5 sentences) says the bedrock changes 'from the coarse white granite to the east to a fine gray schist to the west'. That is crag-wide and mixed, so it decides nothing, but it does not contradict the wall pages.

quote: Good amount of sharp, quartzy, granite boulders.
note: The crag page (6 sentences) is crag-wide on a crag holding two rocks, and its 'granite' is loose, so it decides neither group. Insequartz Boulder (3 sentences): 'A massive and steep quartz Boulder'. Crystal Party (2): 'quartz boulder'. 'Quartz' names a mineral, not a usable rock. The other boulder pages name no rock.

quote: a dangerous giant boulder field is below this metamorphic rock crag
note: Tripoli Road Crag (11 sentences) says only 'metamorphic', which is generic and does not confirm metasedimentary. Bryant Ledge (12 sentences) and Indian Leap Falls (5) name no rock. The area page (WM: Lincoln/Woodstock Area) names no rock.

quote: Questa Dome is a 600-ft tall south-facing granite dome in the secluded Latir Peaks Wilderness
note: Crag page: 13 sentences; it also has 'The granite bouldering along the trail to the Dome is okay too.' Questa Dome proper (area/105979184, 15 sentences): 'beautiful white granite'. Questa Flatiron (area/108377108, 6 sentences): 'a smooth-faced 230' southwest-facing granite formation'. Questa Dome Bouldering (1 sentence): 'Excellent granite bouldering'. The Legs (4 sentences) names no rock; the crag page covers it. Omitted: 'south-facing' for the Questa Dome wall (stated only on the crag-level page); The Legs Sun & Shade 'Routes Mostly Face: Southwest' (hedged).

quote: Like all the rhyolite areas along the East Fork, the rock is a bit crumbly but improves with traffic.
note: Only Los Huevos (4 sentences) names rhyolite. The Subdivisions (1), Best of the Rest (3), Huacas (3), The Roost (3) and Sleeper (1) name no rock, so the group is not fully covered. The parent Las Conchas page names no rock. It calls The Subdivisions south-facing, but that is crag-level and not carried to the walls.

quote: All the rocks are granite (at least I'm pretty sure) so they're all pretty rough.
note: The crag page has 3 sentences, and its statement is hedged ('at least I'm pretty sure'), so it is not usable. The parent Manitoba/Montgomery Trailhead page (5) names no rock.

quote: Off the beaten path for sure
note: BTown (1 sentence), Black Streak Wall (1), Front Wall (1) and Snooze Wall (1) name no rock. Only the parent La Madre North page names one: 'long hillside of limestone cliffs'. That is a parent page only. Warming Wall (area/202926907, a 1-sentence page): 'South facing wall up above and right across the canyon from Snooze wall'.
